_comment: Hand attribution for Hong Kong's unattributed bucket - lines the extractor could not bind to a speaker. Same shape and same applier as the DMS file. A conversation is only listed when the evidence is IN the lines: the speaker's own stage directions, a name they use, or screen furniture with no actor at all. Everything else stays unattributed on purpose.

new_characters.name: Elder Magpie
new_characters.note: The deceased female Whampoa elder and decker whose shop is searched during Grendel. Other dialogue calls her a 'salty old woman' and says that she maintained the shadow-nets. Her one surviving written note is on her own desk.

new_characters.name: Ares Technician Lee
new_characters.note: The Ares Asia employee who signed the maintenance warning on the first-floor power conduit '-Lee'. Kept separate from the unrelated Coda impound quartermaster named Lee.

5536962e3234375434000be4.why: the crew's decker reading a stolen machine: 'She plugs her deck into it and scans the screen'

54d00020306364a06a008a84.why: All three explicit sources are two runtime New Actor party spawners. Their identities vary with the selected team, so no stable character voice exists for these keys.

_terminals_note: Terminal conversations are attributed to the terminal bucket rather than left unattributed, because unattributed lines are invisible to the lab and silent in the pack. Once they are in a container, build_screen_splits.py parses them like any other screen and moves the human-written parts - Dr. Taylor's and Dr. Hardingham's lab notes, the Eastern Tiger development diaries - to the people who wrote them.
